stories.title: US October retail sales match forecasts, but core spending beats them and keeps a December Fed rate rise on track
stories.summary: US retail sales rose 0.2% in October, exactly as forecast, after a big jump in September. But 'core' sales, which leave out cars, gas, building materials and restaurants, rose faster than expected. Markets expect the Fed to raise interest rates in December, and higher rates tend to pull money away from riskier assets like crypto.
points: Retail sales rose 0.2% in October, in line with forecasts, after an unrevised 0.8% in September, per Reuters.
Core sales rose 0.6% against a 0.4% forecast, and September's core figure was revised up to 0.5% from 0.1%, per Reuters.

The Fed's rate range is 3.75%-4.00%, and markets have priced in a quarter-point rise in December, per Reuters citing CME FedWatch. On Monday evening FedWatch showed 90.7% for a 0.25-point rise and 9.3% for 0.5 point, per CryptoTicker. These are market bets, not a Fed decision.
US industrial production fell 0.4% in October against a forecast rise of 0.1%, per The Rio Times.

sources.label: Reuters via Investing.com: US retail sales

stories.title: Bitcoin stuck in the low-to-mid $60,000s after ETF selling pauses; Nvidia reports tonight
stories.summary: Bitcoin is holding in the low-to-mid $60,000s after a hard November. US spot bitcoin funds (ETFs) took in a small amount of new money on Monday, ending a week-long run of withdrawals; one day is not a trend. Crypto has been moving with AI and tech stocks, so tonight's results from Nvidia, the AI chip maker, are the next big test.
points: US spot bitcoin ETFs took in a net $7.99M on Monday, per SoSoValue data reported by KuCoin, ending a seven-day outflow streak. BlackRock's IBIT added $76.5M while Grayscale's GBTC lost $34.6M, per CoinDesk.
Bitcoin fell about 13% over the past week and 20.8% over 30 days, per The Block. It was down nearly 16% for November and 25% for the year as of Monday, per Yahoo Finance.
Nvidia releases results at about 1:20pm PT (4:20pm ET, 04:20 Wednesday Bangkok), with its call at 5pm ET (05:00 Wednesday Bangkok), per Nvidia. It is the first report since CEO Jensen Huang left.
Analysts expect revenue of $109.1B and earnings of $2.47 a share (LSEG, per TheNextWeb); Nvidia's own guidance was $108B plus or minus 2%, per OANDA.

sources.label: The Block: Grayscale on the selloff

stories.title: Fed's Waller skips interest rates and talks stablecoins and tokenized markets
stories.summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller gave a speech today about how blockchain-based money fits into the payments system, with no comments on interest rates. A senior central banker treating stablecoins and tokenization as part of the future system matters for crypto's long-term place, but he also flagged real risks like hacks and lost keys.
points: The speech, 'Considerations at the Intersection of Payments and Tokenized Markets', was given at The Clearing House annual conference, per the Federal Reserve.

Waller said 'a convergence between blockchain technologies and established markets is clearly under way' and that stablecoins 'are starting to be used behind the scenes to settle obligations among participants in card networks', per the Federal Reserve.
He said 'central bank money need not be used in every transaction or on every platform' but remains the system's foundation, per the Federal Reserve.
He warned about smart-contract exploits and lost keys, per the Federal Reserve.

briefs.title: Wallet-swapping code removed from 178 sites
briefs.summary: Optimizely says the flaw is fixed and the injected code that swapped crypto addresses on 178 organizations' sites, including Ledger's, is gone; Ledger says private keys stayed protected, per TokenPost. Always check the first and last characters of any address you paste.
